# AI Industry Event Intelligence API

> Read-only, cache-first API for AI, humanoid robotics, bio, medical-device, and
> digital-health industry events. Domestic Korea coverage spans COEX, KINTEX,
> and the AKEI nationwide exhibition directory; international benchmarks too.
> JSON is canonical; a token-cheaper Markdown rendering is available for prompt
> ingestion. No live LLM generation runs on reads.

Base URL: https://events.nukk.net
Schema version: 0.1 (see GET /api/v1/schema for the field descriptor)

## How to use

- Default response is `application/json`. Each event carries explicit nullable
  fields, a controlled-vocabulary classification, and source provenance.
- For prompt ingestion, request a Markdown table view with `?format=md` or
  `Accept: text/markdown`. Same fields, fewer tokens (keys are not repeated per
  row). `?format=md` takes precedence over the Accept header.
- Collections are keyset-paginated. Follow `page.next_cursor` (opaque) until
  `page.has_more` is false. `limit` defaults to 20 and is clamped to 100.
- Poll for freshness with `updated_since` / `changed_since` (RFC3339), or read
  the field-level change feed at `/api/v1/events/changes`.
- Every enriched claim has provenance: `GET /api/v1/events/{event_id}/sources`.
- Action fields are intended for operational planning. `actions.*` booleans
  default to false when unknown, so check `missing_fields[]` before treating a
  false value as a source-backed absence.

## Quota (keyless, per IP)

- 60 requests / minute
- 2000 requests / day

Exceeding either returns HTTP 429 with a `Retry-After` header.

## Endpoints

- GET /api/v1 — meta index: version, schema_version, endpoints, quota, vocabularies.
- GET /api/v1/schema — v0.1 schema descriptor + supported_versions.
- GET /api/v1/openapi.yaml — OpenAPI 3.x specification.
- GET /api/v1/events — list events. Filters: list=all|venue|benchmark,
  since (start_date >= YYYY-MM-DD), before (start_date <= YYYY-MM-DD),
  active_from + active_before (event date-span overlap), include_undated,
  updated_since, changed_since, category, venue. Pagination: limit, cursor.
  When list=venue and since is omitted, since defaults to today's Asia/Seoul
  date so the domestic venue feed is current/upcoming by default.
  Response also carries category_counts: the per-category event count under the
  active (non-category) filters, in canonical taxonomy order.
- GET /api/v1/events/{event_id} — single event detail with provenance.
- GET /api/v1/events/{event_id}/sources — source provenance entries (>=1).
- GET /api/v1/events/changes — field-level change feed. Filters: since, event_id.

## Vocabularies

- categories: ai, humanoid-robotics, bio, medical-devices, digital-health
- list_kinds: all, venue, benchmark
- venues: coex, kintex (venue ids; domestic events at other venues carry venue name text only)
- update_state: new, unchanged, updated, conflicting
- status: scheduled, tentative, postponed, cancelled, ended

## Notes for agents

- IDs (`event_id`) are durable and stable forever; safe to store and re-fetch.
- `missing_fields[]` lists dotted paths that are null/unknown — treat them as
  honestly absent, not as zero/false.
- Non-taxonomy events stay visible and carry `excluded: true`; do not treat the
  flag as a reason to hide venue schedules.
- Summaries are short source-derived event descriptions from venue detail pages
  when available; absent source descriptions stay null and are listed in
  missing_fields.
- `register_url`, `exhibit_url`, `registration_deadline`,
  `exhibitor_deadline`, and `cost_hint` may come from linked organizer pages;
  use `sources[]` to distinguish organizer-backed facts from venue-only records.
- Some KINTEX events (externally organized hall rentals not yet on the venue's own
  calendar) are discovered via an exhibition aggregator; those carry an
  `aggregator`-type entry in `sources[]`. When the same event is found on both the
  venue and the aggregator, it is collapsed into one record (the venue-sourced one).
